title: Latency Garden — Weekly Handoff and Oncall Notes (2027-05-30)
content:
TL;DR:
- Quiet week for pages but two subtle latency regressions observed in the small-model route (v2-quant). No customer-facing errors, but tail P99 spiked above SLO twice during the Tuesday afternoon traffic burst.
- Oncall handoff checklist updated with quick KV-cache sanity tests and a temporary mitigation we used (soft-evict prefix cache).
- Action items: improve metric granularity for cold-start vs steady-state, ship backpressure knob to platform config, and add a scheduled validation of model binary compatibility.

Incident summary (high level):
1) Tuesday 2027-05-25 14:05-14:42 UTC — "small-model-p99-regress"
   - Symptoms: P99 token latency on route /generate-small climbed from 280ms -> 720ms for ~25 minutes. Error rate stayed <0.1%.
   - Root cause (hypothesis): concurrent KV-cache churn due to a spike in prefix diversity from an internal batch job that hit the hosted API (non-customer). The churn caused nanoseconds-level locks to become contended on the inference worker, amplifying dispatch latency at tail.
   - Mitigation applied: disabled the batch job and toggled soft-evict (reduced cache size by 30% across a node pool). Tail returned to normal within 8 minutes after eviction and worker rotation.
   - Post-incident: created JIRA SRE-4821 to track deterministic repro and long-term fix (better cache eviction heuristics + shed-on-high-contention).

2) Thursday 2027-05-27 03:12-03:28 UTC — "kv-compat-warn"
   - Symptoms: small blips of 500ms+ on some nodes during maintenance window; most requests unaffected.
   - Root cause: a rolling kernel security update restarted a small percentage of nodes; the restart surfaced an incompatibility between the runtime's on-disk KV state and the newer kernel’s IO scheduler timing — led to slightly longer cold cache recovery.
   - Mitigation: delayed remaining OS rollouts, marked affected nodes as unschedulable for inference, and rolled back one node to previous kernel.
   - Follow-up: add kernel/driver compatibility check to the private-deployments upgrade playbook.

SLO snapshot (current week vs target):
- API request latency SLO (P99 <= 500ms): This week 98.5% (target 99.5%) — regression tied to the Tuesday event.
- Error budget remaining (monthly): ~72% remaining. No emergency burn.
- Availability (99.95% monthly): met.

Observability notes / gaps found:
- We need better per-pool P99 decomposition (cache-miss vs dispatch vs kernel latency). Current dashboards only show end-to-end; hard to triage quickly.
- Tracing tags: add kv-cache-eviction and node-kernel-version to request traces for backfills.

Handoff / oncall notes (to next shift):
- Check list on takeover:
  1) Quick pager inbox scan (last 12h) for spikes in p99 and any new incident SRE tickets.
  2) Run `kv-cache-health --pool small-model-v2` (local helper) — expected: cache hit ratio > 92%. If < 85%, move to mitigation steps.
  3) Confirm no ongoing kernel rollouts in the region (kube labels: node-role=inference).
  4) Validate autoscaler headroom: desired queued tokens < 150 per pool.
- If you see a p99 spike:
  - Check for concurrent internal jobs (look at infra/job-run logs).
  - Soft-evict prefix cache on affected pool (gradual 10% steps), watch p99 and errors. Don't hard-evict unless instructed.
  - If contention persists after 20 minutes, open a hotfix PR to adjust dispatch concurrency for that pool and notify platform SLT.

Playbook & runbook notes (work-in-progress):
- Updated runbook steps for "p99-regressions without errors" with the soft-evict procedure and a short checklist for node marking.
- New note to add: when kernel upgrades are planned, run a small canary with `kv-state-checker` against a read-only snapshot to ensure no IO tail anomalies. (PR in github ops-playbooks pending).

Action items (owners + ETA):
- SRE-4821 (Mark Chen) — reproduce the cache-churn scenario in staging and validate eviction heuristics. ETA: 2027-06-07.
- Add per-pool latency decomposition panel (Olivia Gomez) — dashboard PR and alert tuning. ETA: 2027-06-03.
- Backfill node kernel compatibility test into private-deployments upgrade playbook (Samir Rao) — include step to snapshot kv-state. ETA: 2027-06-10.
- Small immediate improvement: ship `trace-tag:kv-evict` with next runtime deploy (Aisha) — ETA: 2027-06-02.

Notes to self / informal thoughts:
- We keep seeing edge cases where internal batch jobs mimic customer traffic and expose infra weaknesses. We should add an internal traffic classification label at the ingress so we can throttle internal-sender agent or route it to a lower-priority queue.
- Consider a short experiment: reduce default prefix-KV retention for non-critical pools for 24h and measure p99 variance. Might be a cheap mitigation.

Meeting agenda for Monday SRE sync:
- 10m: Walk through Tuesday incident timeline and current repro hypothesis.
- 15m: Dashboard update proposal and alert thresholds.
- 15m: Private deploy upgrade playbook kernel test and rollout window policy.
- 10m: Quick wins and action assignment.

References & links:
- Confluence: SRE-Latency-Garden-Runbook (link above)
- Jira: SRE-4821 (ticket for reproducer)
- Slack threads: #sre-ops `thread: tX2p4` (internal batch job callout)
- GitHub: ops-playbooks PR #58 (soft-evict procedure)

End of notes.

-- Aisha
